status: exploratory (pre-registered criterion; one fitted model for move SIZE)
hypothesis: The size of the coming move is predictable where its direction is not (E003, E008, E007 side-finding). A small L2 logistic regression on recent volatility, trade intensity and the clock predicts whether |return over H| will exceed a fixed threshold, stably out-of-sample under walk-forward validation, and its stated probabilities carry rank information about the realised move size.
acceptance_criterion: PRE-REGISTERED. On the concatenated out-of-sample predictions of the expanding walk-forward (purge = H, embargo 24h, quarterly test blocks, >= 365 training days), the model 'predicts move size at horizon H' only if ALL hold in BOTH exploration-OOS (before 2024) and validation-OOS (2024-01 -> 2025-06): (1) Brier at least 5% below the period's own base-rate Brier (a hindsight benchmark, therefore strict); (2) large/small call accuracy at least 5 percentage points above the naive rate max(base, 1-base); (3) Spearman rank correlation between the stated probability and the realised |return| >= 0.10 with the block-bootstrap 95% interval excluding zero. Reported but NOT a pass condition: ECE and the reliability table (calibration is Phase 11's job). Three horizons = three separate tests (1h, 6h, 24h), not a search. Rolling layout is a robustness check, never used to choose. TRIPWIRE: accuracy > 0.80 or rho > 0.60 is treated as suspicious (E003's strongest fit-free value was 0.45) and investigated before being recorded.

model.type: logistic regression, L2 penalty, C = 0.1 (fixed in advance, same as E011, no search)
model.preprocessing: log-transform of the six positive ratio inputs (a value of exactly 0 -- a candle with no trades -- is treated as missing), then StandardScaler fitted on each fold's training rows only

target.definition: large_move: 1 if |return over H| > threshold_H, else 0 (sign ignored)
target.how_thresholds_were_fixed: round numbers near the exploration-period median |return| (0.272% / 0.666% / 1.625%), written down before any model was run; the validation base rate is lower (0.475 / 0.408 / 0.452 vs 0.528 / 0.461 / 0.525) because 2024-25 is calmer -- a test of whether the model follows the regime
target.outcome: close of candle opening at as_of+H

dataset.source: E001 replay index + candle-derived features (volatility, microstructure, calendar)

validation_design: expanding walk-forward, min_train 365d, test blocks 90d, purge H, embargo 24h; rolling 730d as robustness

6h_expanding.note: fails criterion (2) in validation by 0.4 points; everything else passes

results: PASS at 1h (both layouts), NO PASS at 6h and 24h. 1h: the model's stated probability of a >0.25% move has rank correlation 0.45 (exploration) / 0.36 (validation) with the realised move size, Brier 15% / 9% better than the base rate, large/small calls right 65.6% / 62.5% of the time vs 50.6% / 52.5% naive; ECE 0.013 / 0.040 before any calibration. 6h is a near-miss (fails only the +5-point accuracy bar in validation, by 0.4 points; Brier +8%, rho 0.33) -- recorded as no pass, not re-tested. 24h weakens clearly in validation (Brier +3%, accuracy +2.4 pp) though rho stays positive (0.21).
consistent_across_time: 1h: accuracy beats naive in 7 of 8 years by +3 to +13 points; 2021 is the one negative year (-1.7) in every run and horizon -- the year the threshold label's base rate was highest (persistently volatile), so the hindsight naive rate is hard to beat. Validation (2024-25, calmer) is weaker than exploration everywhere but still passes at 1h.
leakage_check: Bench verified in E010; fold gaps = H + 24 + 1 on every fold except where a data hole widens them. rho 0.45 equals E003's fit-free value for tr_mean_14_rel alone (0.45), so the fitted model adds little beyond the strongest single input -- consistent with no leak and with a genuine, well-known volatility-clustering effect.
overfitting_suspected: Low: 9 inputs, C = 0.1, 56k rows, coefficient signs stable in 89-100% of folds for the five largest; performance degrades gracefully with horizon rather than collapsing.
affected_design: Phase 11 calibrates the 1h move-size model on a purged calibration slice (raw vs Platt vs isotonic, reliability with intervals). 6h and 24h stay reported near-miss/no-pass; not calibrated. This is an UNCERTAINTY output (how big the next move may be), never a direction.
notes: Six runs (3 horizons x expanding/rolling), all reported. If this passes, Phase 11 calibrates it on a purged calibration slice; if it fails, the honest output is 'no calibrated uncertainty either'. Nothing about the live system changes regardless of outcome.
